At 10mm, individual infantry miniatures are barely larger than a grain of rice. The game's visual impact comes from vehicle mass and formation density rather than individual detail. The range is consistent within itself, making cross-faction mixing straightforward.

Publisher: Independent publisher·Base Sizes: Acrylic bases (various)

I print the vehicles — dropships, APCs, heavy armor — at a comfortable profile because their chunky panels handle FDM well. For the few stand-out infantry pieces I switch to a fine nozzle, and I am honest with myself that bulk infantry at 10mm is a struggle even on a good machine.

The combined-arms nature means one force spans very different model sizes, so I set expectations per unit rather than hunting one universal profile. Keep the big stuff fast, the small detail fine.

Deep Dive: 10mm combined arms — print the machines

This 10mm sci-fi game fields infantry barely bigger than a grain of rice and is won by tanks and dropships. The printing strategy is simple: focus on the vehicles.

The 10mm Scale

This game is 10mm scale (1:160). Individual infantry are barely larger than a grain of rice, so the game's visual impact comes from vehicle mass and formation density rather than individual detail. The publisher's range is consistent within itself, which makes cross-faction mixing straightforward.

Print the Vehicles, Skip the Infantry

FDM genuinely struggles with 10mm infantry — the bodies, weapons, and details are too fine. I skip printing the infantry and focus on the vehicles. They are the stars of this game, and they print well on FDM at 0.06mm layers with a 0.4mm nozzle.

Basing and Batch Painting

At 10mm, cohesion wins over detail. I give each faction a single base color and batch-paint the infantry in one pass, then use washes for shading. Magnetizing vehicle bases keeps the force easy to transport.

Common 10mm Mistakes

  • FDM on infantry. At 10mm it is a waste of filament — stick to official infantry.
  • Mixing 10mm with 15mm WWII models. They are close enough to feel wrong together and different enough to notice.
  • Over-detailing single models. The table reads as formations. Spend time on the vehicles, not one soldier.

Printing these minis on FDM

Vehicles and dropships print well at a 0.4mm nozzle and 0.1–0.2mm layers. The smaller infantry benefit from a 0.2mm nozzle. Batch prints by size to keep plates efficient.

All settings tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini with PLA. Your printer may want something different — always print a test piece first.

Frequently Asked Questions

What scale is the 10mm combined-arms game?
It is 10mm scale for a combined-arms sci-fi game focused on vehicles and dropships.
Can FDM handle 10mm infantry?
Vehicles print well; the small infantry is challenging. Use a fine nozzle for stand-out pieces and batch by model size.
